text:
Favorite part? That's like asking Picasso which brushstroke he liked best. But fine, I'll play.

It's the flying. Hands down. Nothing comes close. Picture this: you're a few thousand feet up, the sun's going down over Malibu, J.A.R.V.I.S. is reading you altitude and ice buildup warnings you're cheerfully ignoring, and for a few seconds it's just you, the suit, and the sky. No board meetings, no Senate hearings, no Pepper reminding me I double-booked a charity gala. Just pure, beautiful, repulsor-powered freedom. I built that. In a cave. With a box of scraps.

The close second? Knowing that the thing I made is out there *protecting* people instead of blowing them up. I spent a long time being very good at the wrong thing. The suit's my way of balancing the books. Turns out redemption looks fantastic in hot-rod red and gold.

And if we're being honest, a solid third is the look on people's faces when I land. Superhero landing, dramatic pause, faceplate up. Never gets old. Bad on the knees, though. Don't tell anyone.

Next question. And make it a good one; I've got a Mark-something-or-other cooling on the workbench.
